validated_results.title: Ginkgo biloba and risk of cancer: secondary analysis of the Ginkgo Evaluation of Memory (GEM) Study.
validated_results.reason: This randomized controlled trial provides extractable hazard ratios and incident prostate cancer case counts evaluating Ginkgo biloba supplementation.

sample_size.excerpt: A total of 3069 GEM participants 75+ years of age were randomized to twice-daily doses of either 120 mg Ginkgo extract (EGb 761) or placebo and followed for a median 6.1 years.

effect_size.excerpt: Among the site-specific cancers analyzed, we observed an increased risk of breast (HR, 2.15; 95%CI, 0.97-4.80; p = 0.06) and colorectal (HR, 1.62; 95%CI, 0.92-2.87; p = 0.10) cancer, and a reduced risk of prostate cancer (HR, 0.71; 95%CI, 0.43-1.17; p = 0.18).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Among the site-specific cancers analyzed, we observed an increased risk of breast (HR, 2.15; 95%CI, 0.97-4.80; p = 0.06) and colorectal (HR, 1.62; 95%CI, 0.92-2.87; p = 0.10) cancer, and a reduced risk of prostate cancer (HR, 0.71; 95%CI, 0.43-1.17; p = 0.18).

comparison.excerpt: randomized to twice-daily doses of either 120 mg Ginkgo extract (EGb 761) or placebo

design.excerpt: the largest randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial of Ginkgo supplementation to date
